scenario: For our assembly line quality checks, we need a vision model that catches defects quickly enough so it won't slow down the main conveyor belt during peak shifts.
Wildlife camera traps need to run for months on one battery, but they also have to tell the difference between a rare leopard and a stray dog in bad lighting.
Our robotic arms need to stop immediately if a human gets too close, but they also can't stop every time a shadow passes over the sensor or production stops entirely.
The automated tutor needs to explain math steps clearly so kids actually learn, but it also has to run on the cheap tablets the school district bought.
Delivery route optimization has to reroute around accidents without making drivers take weird detours that drain their EV batteries.
Solar grid forecasting has to be right about sudden cloud cover, but the model running on the local panels can't be too heavy or the processor overheats.
We want an endpoint malware scanner that catches new ransomware variants without slowing down employee computers during normal work hours.

On battery-backed port cranes, the vision module must identify people or obstacles dependably and react before the crane reaches the unsafe zone, without consuming so much charge that auxiliary systems lose reserve capacity.

Marine scientists should receive trustworthy coral-bleaching maps from months-long reef deployments without exhausting buoy power or turning large image uploads into an environmentally heavy workflow. The edge system should make dependable local assessments and send only what is needed for research review.

With rescue drones limited to one field battery, onboard scene analysis must preserve enough charge for the full search, identify people and hazards dependably, and finish each pass before the aircraft reaches the next sector.

A historic museum uses wireless sensors to decide which rooms genuinely need conservation staff attention, so spurious warnings create real disruption. The gateways have a very small electrical allowance, and the museum wants background analysis to stay consistent with its low-impact operations policy instead of depending on fossil-heavy overflow.

A museum lends visitors handheld translation devices that should update speech quickly enough to feel like a conversation. The units must last through a full day of tours, and the museum would rather schedule heavy preparation work when its building is on cleaner supply than add more charging demand during fossil-heavy peaks.

A pop-up music festival wants crowd-density maps refreshed often enough for stewards to react while a bottleneck is forming. The temporary network runs from battery trailers, and organizers want to minimize generator use overnight rather than keep extra machines humming between updates.

Technicians should isolate a failing wind-turbine component before it causes a costly shutdown, while nacelle sensors continue operating through long service intervals. The local diagnostic service should recognise genuine fault signatures, return a maintenance indication promptly, and avoid processor use that unnecessarily drains the embedded power supply.

A seafood plant uses a camera to spot broken seals on vacuum packs. Wrong calls are costly, the decision has to arrive before the pack leaves the inspection point, and the edge box cannot draw so much that it overheats in the chilled room.

In a printing house, operators want the camera to catch a wrong page insert before the book is bound. It needs to make a solid call in time to pause the line, without forcing the inspection unit onto a larger power supply.

Rescue crews should be directed to the right building section within moments after an earthquake, even when drones must remain aloft on limited batteries. The onboard search service needs dependable victim indications, quick scene interpretation, and restrained processor use so aircraft can keep surveying instead of returning early to recharge.

Inside an ambulance, the ECG assistant has to give crews a dependable warning while there is still time to act, yet it runs on the same portable unit used for the rest of the trip. Long transfers and spotty charging mean it cannot burn through the device battery just to respond faster.

An insurer is preparing a storm-response service that prioritizes incoming property claims for adjusters. The ordering should be dependable and available while field teams are still allocating visits, and large cloud processing jobs should use lower-impact regions or periods when that does not delay the response.

A warehouse robot should stop or reroute before a worker steps into its path, while still completing a full shift between charges. Its onboard perception must distinguish people and obstacles dependably, react within the safety window, and avoid sustained heavy computation that shortens operating time.
